# S-3 · Control Allocation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | S Select (system level) |
| Phases | PH-TMRR (primary) |
| Depends on | S-2, P-17 |
| Inputs | ART-BASELINE, ART-BND, ART-ORG-CONTEXT, ART-REQ, ART-CAT, ART-INV, ART-RA, ART-SD, EXT-ORG-POLICY, EXT-PRODUCT |
| Outputs | ART-BASELINE (updates) |
| Writes facts | — |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-ISSE, PER-ISSM, PER-PRIV, PER-ISSO · A: PER-PM · C: PER-CIO, PER-AO, PER-SPONSOR, PER-CISO, PER-CCP · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PER-ISSE](../../personas/PER-ISSE.md), [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-ISSO](../../personas/PER-ISSO.md), [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-CIO](../../personas/PER-CIO.md), [PER-AO](../../personas/PER-AO.md), [PER-SPONSOR](../../personas/PER-SPONSOR.md), [PER-CISO](../../personas/PER-CISO.md), [PER-CCP](../../personas/PER-CCP.md) |

Purpose: Designate controls as system-specific, hybrid or common and allocate them to system elements, so the preliminary design (RV-PDR) shows where each control lives.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** S-2 is done (`tailoring.yaml` written, `baseline.json` current), and
   ART-REQ records P-17's allocation of requirements (`touched_by` includes P-17, or ART-REQ
   is seeded). Why: controls are allocated from the tailored baseline and the allocated
   requirements (SP 800-37r2 Task S-3).
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`. List the tailored baseline's controls with
   `uv run rmf catalog show --run <run> --fields title`, and the components from
   `artifacts/data/boundary.yaml` (`CMP-*` IDs). Note each common control provider and what
   it offers, from ART-ORG-CONTEXT and the `## Common controls available for inheritance`
   section of ART-BASELINE.
3. **Interview** PER-ISSE first (architecture: which component provides each capability),
   then PER-ISSM (the designation of each control), and PER-CCP for the controls a provider
   covers fully or in part. Ask, per family, rather than per control. Why: allocation is a
   design decision; the engineer knows where a capability lives, the provider what it
   delivers.
4. **Designate and allocate each control.** For every control in `baseline.json`:
   - **type:** `common` (the provider implements it and the system inherits it),
     `hybrid` (partly the provider, partly the system), or `system-specific`;
   - **components:** the `CMP-*` components that implement the system's part. Allocate a
     control only to the components that need the capability, not to every component (an
     audit-log control goes to the log server, not to each sensor). Use `this-system` only
     when the control is organizational or procedural with no component home;
   - **provider:** for `common` and `hybrid`, the provider's name as ART-ORG-CONTEXT gives
     it;
   - **sources:** the answer or architecture passage behind the allocation.
   A control the provider's offer does not fully meet becomes `hybrid` with the system's
   supplement allocated to components. Why: SP 800-37r2 Task S-3 allocates controls to
   system elements consistent with the architecture and the allocated requirements.
5. **Write `artifacts/data/allocation.yaml`** whole (schema
   `framework/schema/allocation.schema.json`), one record per baseline control:

   ```yaml
   allocations:
     - control_id: au-2
       type: hybrid
       components: [CMP-GW-OS, CMP-COLLECTOR]
       provider: "Installation Cybersecurity Service Provider"
       sources: [INT-016.A3, ART-ORG-CONTEXT]
   ```

   Work family by family for a large baseline, but write the file once, whole, after the
   last family. If the file was seeded, keep its records and add the missing controls.
   Each record also lists `requirements`: the REQ-## IDs of ART-REQ the control is
   intended to satisfy. Every requirement must be named by at least one control (TLR-009).
   Add one `providers` record per common control provider an allocation names:

   ```yaml
   providers:
     - provider: "Installation Cybersecurity Service Provider"
       determination:
         by: [PER-PM, PER-AODR]
         commensurate: true
         parameters_examined: true
         implementation_info: [ART-ORG-CONTEXT]
         sources: [INT-016.A4]
   ```

   The system owner (PER-PM) and the AO, or the AO's designated representative (PER-AODR),
   determine whether the provider's controls protect
   this system commensurate with its risk, after examining the control parameters, not
   just the control IDs, and reading the provider's current implementation information and
   assessment results. A provider not found commensurate supplies no `common` control:
   make the control `hybrid` and allocate the system's part (TLR-010).
6. **Cross-check the requirements.** Every requirement ART-REQ allocates to a system
   element maps to at least one control allocated to that element; every requirement
   allocated to a common control provider maps to a `common` or `hybrid` control from that
   provider. A gap is a NOTE for S-2 (supplementation) or the provider, not something S-3
   changes in `tailoring.yaml`.
7. **Update `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`.** Append `S-3` to `touched_by` and rewrite the
   allocation part of `## Tailoring and allocation`: the count of common, hybrid and
   system-specific controls, each provider and what it covers, the components with the most
   controls, and any requirement gap from step 6, traced. Keep every other section.
8. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-3`,
   until 0 errors.
9. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-ISSE | responsible (R) | which components provide each security capability; controls that need no allocation to some components |
| PER-ISSM | responsible (R) | designation of each control as common, hybrid or system-specific |
| PER-CCP | consulted (C) | what the provider implements for this system, fully or in part, and its authorization status |
| PER-PRIV (when PII is processed) | responsible (R) | allocation of the privacy controls and privacy-related requirements |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects PER-ISSE and PER-ISSM interviews.

## Inputs

- `baseline.json` (the tailored baseline; generated, read only)
- `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`, `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-BND.md`, `artifacts/data/boundary.yaml` (components)
- `artifacts/ART-ORG-CONTEXT.md` (common control providers)
- `artifacts/ART-REQ.md` (requirements allocated to the system, its elements and the
  environment)
- `artifacts/data/allocation.yaml`, when seeded
- Control titles: `uv run rmf catalog show --run <run> --fields title`

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts/data/allocation.yaml` | — | schema `allocation`, written whole |
| `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md` | `touched_by: [S-1, S-2, S-3]` | updated (updater) |

## Facts

S-3 writes no facts.

## Done when

- `allocation.yaml` gives every baseline control a type, at least one component and
  sources; `common` and `hybrid` records name the provider.
- ART-BASELINE lists S-3 in `touched_by` and summarizes the allocation.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-3` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task S-3`, with the count per type and per provider.
- A requirement gap from step 6 is a NOTE naming the requirement and the missing control.
